title: Tales of Xillia 2
subtitle: A family can decide the fate of another world

body: Tales of Xillia 2 is Bandai Namco's PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 1 November 2012. Ludger Will Kresnik becomes involved in the destruction of parallel dimensions, using a family ability that gives him access to worlds whose continued existence has consequences elsewhere. Characters and places from the earlier game return around this new protagonist. The premise turns a familiar sequel journey into a problem of choices, asking what responsibility belongs to somebody whose actions can determine which version of a life is allowed to continue.

Exploration connects towns, conversations and encounters with visible enemies, while battles move the party into a separate action space. Returning companions bring their own histories into the group, and voiced skits allow those relationships to develop between major events. Ludger's role gives the player another way to approach the combat while the broader linking structure remains recognisable. The journey therefore combines familiarity with a new centre of attention. Known people become companions to somebody else, allowing their previous experiences to sit beside the problems introduced by the Kresnik family and its unusual power.

Kenji Anabuki and Asana Inoki directed, with Hideo Baba producing and Motoi Sakuraba composing the score. Character designs again draw on Kōsuke Fujishima and Mutsumi Inomata, with Daigo Okumura contributing to the cast. North American and European editions followed in August 2014. The game's theme places choice at the centre of the future being constructed. Its sequel structure supports that idea by returning to a world the player may already value, then presenting alternative versions whose people and relationships make a decision harder to treat as an abstract solution.
